No substantive policy content relevant to Chapter 5B economic governance questions.","exclusion_reason":"Navigation/boilerplate content with no substantive policy or factual content about economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Unit-0002 describes López Obrador's third 2018 presidential campaign agenda including 'austeridad republicana' (reorienting public resources from operating costs to investment), social programs targeting poverty and vulnerable populations, 'erradicación' of political corruption 'dando ejemplo' (setting an example from the top), and promised infrastructure improvements (gasoline, refineries). Also mentions his 'austerity republic' principle for redirecting spending. Material for 5B.1 (sustained prosperity agenda) and 5B.7 (corruption elimination promise).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0002","unit-0004"],"explanation":"Unit-0003 covers López Obrador's 2012 presidential program: deep democratic cleansing to end the 'neoporfirista regime of corruption, impunity and privileges'; promises to halt 'neoliberalism that creates inequalities'; guarantees protection of state oil company Pemex from privatization; and criticizes 'false alternation' between PRI and PAN. Shows his stated economic policy direction and critiques predecessor administrations. Relevant to 5B.1, 5B.7, and 5B.10.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.4","5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0005"],"explanation":"Unit-0004 covers MORENA's 2012 founding and policy opposition to Peña Nieto's structural reforms (energy, education, labor, telecommunications). López Obrador condemned the EPN executive as corrupt, weak, and incompetent regarding military drug war, basic goods price increases, and response to Trump. Describes his 'hostility' to structural reforms. Relevant to 5B.1, 5B.2, 5B.4, 5B.7, and 5B.10 as it documents his stated opposition to economic liberalization reforms.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0004","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Unit-0005 presents the 2018 campaign Project 2018 economic program in detail: 'austeridad republicana' (reorient public resources from operating costs to investment without raising taxes), social attention to poverty and human development of vulnerable populations, energy self-sufficiency via increased domestic gasoline production, food self-sufficiency via guaranteed prices for local producers, corruption eradication by 'giving example' from Los Pinos, and defense of migrants. This is the most detailed economic policy statement in the source and is directly relevant to 5B.1 (prosperity vs rents), 5B.3 (macroeconomic/fiscal rules), 5B.4 (competition/entrepreneurship), 5B.6 (infrastructure/budget quality), 5B.7 (transparency), 5B.8 (fair distribution), 5B.9 (shock management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Unit-0006 describes López Obrador's platform as 'pragmatic social democracy' assuming orthodox free market principles (macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, peso floatation) combined with rejection of privatization and prioritization of national production. It also covers his promise to address corruption without vengeance ('no voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel') and his more conservative positions on social issues. Also covers his December 2018 inauguration actions including National Peace and Security Plan with Guardia Nacional and conditional amnesty for drug traffickers. Relevant to 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.7, 5B.10.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.9","5B.1","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0006","unit-0008"],"explanation":"Unit-0007 covers migration caravans at the US-Mexico border under Trump, López Obrador's offer of work visas to migrants (solidarity response), and Trump's November 26, 2018 threat to 'permanently' close the border (which would cause enormous commercial damage to Mexico). Relevant to 5B.9 (shock management - external/commodity/shock context) and also to 5B.1 and 5B.7 regarding policy responses to external shocks.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0008 is primarily biographical narrative covering López Obrador's childhood, family background, his brother's accidental death at age 15, and the family's relocation. Contains no substantive policy content related to economic governance questions.","exclusion_reason":"Early biographical content (family background, childhood relocation) with no economic policy content relevant to 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0009 covers López Obrador's university enrollment at UNAM in 1972 and his initial political activities through PRI party work and appointment to state government positions under Governor Leandro Rovirosa Wade. Entirely about early career and party political work, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Early PRI career and party political activities, no economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0010 covers López Obrador's PRI career progression including his work at COPLAMAR (poverty zones program), his university teaching at Universidad Autónoma de Tabasco, marriage, and his role in Enrique González Pedrero's 1982 gubernatorial campaign. No substantive economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Continued early career narrative and personal family content, no economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0011 covers López Obrador's role as Tabasco PRI president (1983), his ideological reputation as a dogmatic leftist, his 1984 removal and relocation to Mexico City, and his 1986 book publication. Contains no substantive economic governance policy content for the 5B questions.","exclusion_reason":"Internal party political career narrative, removal from PRI post, book publication - no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0012 covers López Obrador's university graduation (1987), his joining the Democratic Current within PRI, and the 1988 presidential and gubernatorial elections in Tabasco with allegations of fraud. This is pre-presidential political history with no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Political party formation and electoral history narrative, no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0013 covers PRD founding (May 1989), López Obrador's role as Tabasco PRD president, and his 1991-1992 'exodus for democracy' march from Villahermosa to Mexico City. Electoral protest history, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Party founding and protest march narrative, no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0014 covers López Obrador's 1994 Tabasco gubernatorial campaign loss to Roberto Madrazo (PRI) and his protest campaign including a second march to Mexico City and creation of a National Democratic Alliance. Electoral protest history, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral protest and opposition history, no substantive economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0015 covers López Obrador's 1994 book 'Entre la historia y la esperanza', his election as PRD National Executive Committee president in July 1996 with 73.9% of votes, and party context. Internal party leadership, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Party presidency election and book publication, no economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0016 covers PRD electoral successes (1997 DF head of government, state governorships 1997-1999), internal party disputes, Pablo Gómez's interim presidency, and PRD's 1999 electoral chaos requiring vote annulment. Party politics and electoral results, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Party electoral victories and internal disputes, no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0017 covers López Obrador's research publication on FOBAPROA (banking rescue fund), which he described as 'the biggest fraud in history after the Conquest', and his 1999 DF primary campaign. Political research and campaign narrative, not economic governance evaluation.","exclusion_reason":"Political research publication and primary campaign narrative, no substantive economic governance evaluation."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0017","unit-0019"],"explanation":"Unit-0018 covers López Obrador's July 2000 election as DF head of government with 34.5% of votes, his December 2000 inauguration, and the subsequent 2000-2005 period where he 'cemented popular bases' of power. Notes his reputation for 'austerity' (simple apartment, utilitarian car), commitment to accountability and transparency, and his 'mañaneras' morning press conferences. Relevant to 5B.1 (austerity claims), 5B.7 (transparency and accountability), and 5B.10 (economic trajectory).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0018","unit-0020"],"explanation":"Unit-0019 covers López Obrador's DF government results: vigorous public works campaign for urban infrastructure improvement; social protection programs including the 'Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores' (Universal Food Pension for the Elderly). The municipality refused to implement the federal Popular Insurance program, claiming DF residents already received free coverage from municipal institutions. Opposition (PAN) accused the government of populist budget waste. Relevant to 5B.1 (social programs vs patronage), 5B.6 (infrastructure vs announcements), 5B.7 (transparency), 5B.8 (social distribution).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0020 covers López Obrador's public image and communication style: 'pejelagarto' nickname, 'AMLO' acronym, his perceived deficiencies as an orator compared to university-educated opponents, and his intensive use of media including 'mañaneras' press conferences. Personality and communication style analysis, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Political personality and communication style descriptions, not economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0020","unit-0022"],"explanation":"Unit-0021 briefly mentions budget debt growth under López Obrador's DF government - slower than under previous governments, per the text - and assessments of crime-fighting results. Relevant to 5B.6 (budget quality) and 5B.8 (fiscal management), though the information is incidental to the main narrative.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0021","unit-0023"],"explanation":"Unit-0022 covers the March 2004 'videoescándalo' in which prominent PRD politicians and López Obrador's close collaborators (Gustavo Ponce Meléndez, René Bejarano Martínez, Carlos Ímaz Gispert) were filmed in compromising situations including negotiating political favors and handling large cash bundles from businessman Carlos Ahumada. This is a pivotal corruption incident directly relevant to 5B.5 (anti-corruption rule enforcement) and 5B.7 (reliable information and accountability).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0022","unit-0024"],"explanation":"Unit-0023 continues the videoescándalo coverage: corruption charges against involved PRD officials including Rosario Robles (PRD president 2002-2003) and Leonel Godoy (PRD president); López Obrador was not directly implicated but 'difficult to imagine he wasn't aware' of close associate Bejarano's activities. López Obrador's reaction was late and weak - he attributed it to a 'conspiracy' by Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox administration. Directly relevant to 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement against politically connected actors) and 5B.7 (publishing reliable information vs denial/scapegoating).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0024 covers the May 2004 desafuero (parliamentary removal of immunity) request by the PGR against López Obrador related to a minor land expropriation dispute in Cuajimalpa dating from 2000-2001. Political-legal battle over immunity from prosecution, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Legal immunity challenge (desafuero) related to land expropriation dispute, not economic governance policy content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0025 covers the August 2004 demonstration of 200,000 PRD members supporting López Obrador, his October 2004 book 'Un proyecto alternativo de nación', the November 2004 removal of Marcelo Ebrard as DF Security Secretary by President Fox, and the spring 2005 legal battle over immunity. These are all political/legal events surrounding the desafuero, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Political mobilizations, book publication, and security secretary removal - political/legal events not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0026 covers the April 7, 2005 congressional vote approving desafuero (360-127), López Obrador's subsequent civil resistance movement and mass protests, and the Assembly's constitutional challenge to the Supreme Court. Political-legal process, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero congressional vote and subsequent civil resistance mobilization, political/legal process not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0027 covers the May 2005 resolution (PGR unable to get a judge to initiate proceedings), Fox's acceptance of the prosecutor's resignation, and the May 4, 2005 dropping of charges and archive of the case following a 20-minute meeting between Fox and López Obrador. Legal resolution of desafuero case, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Legal resolution of desafuero case, political accommodation between Fox and López Obrador, not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0028 covers López Obrador's July 2005 request for leave as DF head of government, his uncontested PRD presidential primary nomination, and the December 2005 rally where he proclaimed his candidacy. Campaign launch activities, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Presidential candidacy nomination and proclamation rally, campaign launch activities not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0029 covers López Obrador's 2006 presidential campaign positioning against Calderón and PAN, the 'FeCal' insult, and accusations of nepotism, abuse of functions, and influence peddling regarding Calderón's BANOBRAS and Energy Secretary roles. Campaign rhetoric and accusations, not substantive economic governance evidence.","exclusion_reason":"Campaign positioning and electoral accusations, not substantive economic governance policy evidence."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0029","unit-0031"],"explanation":"Unit-0030 covers the 2006 campaign platform of the 'Por el Bien de Todos' coalition: ending the 'privilege, corruption and looting' system; combating tax fraud and evasion; halving presidential salary; social programs for vulnerable populations; investigating FOBAPROA through a Truth Commission; and rejecting neoliberal policies. 'Primero los pobres' (poor first) slogan. Directly relevant to 5B.1 (prosperity agenda), 5B.3 (fiscal/tax rules), 5B.5 (anti-corruption), 5B.7 (accountability/transparency), 5B.8 (distribution of gains/burdens).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0030","unit-0032"],"explanation":"Unit-0031 covers 2006 campaign economic promises: savings from government austerity (100 billion pesos first year) plus new fiscal revenues funding social development programs and productive activities (agriculture, tourism, public works); constitutional right to 'fair' and 'dignified' minimum wage (unspecified amount); energy sector only efficiency reforms, no privatization; agricultural protection through NAFTA chapter revisions. Relevant to 5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.10.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0032 covers López Obrador's denial of connections to Venezuelan President Chávez and distance from the Bolivarian strategy for Latin America. Foreign policy positioning and distancing from Chávez, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"International relations positioning and denial of Chávez connections, not economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0033 covers the July 2006 election night and PREP preliminary results showing a 0.64% Calderón lead, and international election monitoring missions confirming the cleanliness of the process. Electoral process and results, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Election night results and international monitoring confirmation, electoral process not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0034 covers the TEPJF partial recount decision (August 5, 2006) and López Obrador's continued rejection of the ruling, calls for intensified resistance against the 'spurious' Calderón. Electoral dispute continuation, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Continued electoral dispute and resistance mobilization, political process not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0035","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0035 covers the TEPJF partial recount results (August 28, 2006) confirming Calderón's 0.56% victory, and López Obrador's furious reaction calling Calderón a 'usurper'. Electoral dispute, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral recount results and post-electoral reaction, political dispute not economic governance."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0036","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0036 covers the September 1, 2006 PRD congressional protest blocking Fox's annual address, and the September 5 TEPJF validation of elections with Calderón's 233,831-vote margin.
